problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-9x-3y+3z \\ -12x-4y+4z \\ 6x+8y+10z\end{aligned}].$ Find $\,\text{Ker}(T).$

activity_context.topic_title: The Kernel of a Linear Transformation

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Kernel of a Linear Transformation
examples.worked_solution:
Finding the kernel of $\mathbf{T}$ is equivalent to finding the null space of the standard matrix of $\mathbf{T}.$

For the given linear transformation, the standard matrix is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071281/assets/5fa2e7ff6cfc27fce7698124fb835abf5c6f02221ba7c7ebb0b371fef6d3c15a.png)

Setting ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071281/assets/f9fc80048a348773c656ec98ac9299eb1c611bfb07eee747b883eb7398dc295f.png) we then need to solve the equation $T\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.$ First, we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x,$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$

From the first equation, we get 

$$
x=-2y.
$$

 

Therefore, the kernel of the linear transformation $\,\mathbf{T}$ is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071281/assets/cace77f13c7ef817cfefaab742bdca008b29a177b0783dc761bc24d8a1273af3.png)

feedback.problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-8x+4y \\ 6x-3y \\ 2x-y\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $\,u=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ k \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,u\in \text{Ker}(T).$
feedback.worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

So, we need to solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(u) & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}-8\cdot 3+4\cdot k \\ 6\cdot 3-3\cdot k \\ 2\cdot 3-k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-24+4k \\ 18-3k \\ 6-k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-24+4k=0 \\ 18-3k=0 \\ 6-k=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to all three of these equations is $k=6.$
